Build's clean now, exit code 0.

Two of those warnings turned out to be real bugs from the bump, not noise:

1. `src/core/options.js` was still reading `options.retries`, but the new bundler hands options as `retryCount`. That read `undefined.toFixed(0)` and threw.
2. `src/net/retryPolicy.js` treated an unset backoff flag as invalid and threw, but the new config loader leaves unset flags as `undefined` instead of `false`. It now treats `undefined` the same as `false` (disabled).

The rest — `Buffer()`, `fs.exists`, `punycode`, the sync loader hook, `module.parent` — are just deprecation noise from Node itself, not from your code. Build finishes with 8 warnings, 0 errors.
